# Home page

Page type: home

Larkspur Supply Co. is a member-owned outdoor gear cooperative at 214 Alder Street, Port Wren. This is its home page.

Site navigation: Shop, Rentals, Workshops, About, Contact.

Headline: Gear for every season, owned by the people who use it.
Lead: We sell, rent, and repair equipment for hiking, paddling, and winter travel. Members get a dividend every spring.
Call to action: Become a member (links to /join).

Featured this week (three items, each with a photo, name, price, and link):
- Ridgeline 40 L pack, $189, /shop/ridgeline-40 (photo: a green backpack on a granite ledge)
- Tidewater touring kayak rental, $55 per day, /rentals/tidewater (photo: a yellow kayak on a calm bay)
- Hearth canister stove, $74, /shop/hearth-stove (photo: a small stove boiling water)

Upcoming workshops: Map and compass basics (Saturday 8 November 2026, 10:00), Winter layering (Thursday 13 November 2026, 18:30).

Footer: address, phone (360) 555-0142, opening hours Monday–Saturday 9:00–19:00, Sunday 10:00–17:00, and a copyright line: © 2026 Larkspur Supply Co..

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/htmlverify/eval/results/2026-10-18-pilot-abc/home/B-1/work/.claude/skills/htmlverify # htmlverify htmlverify checks HTML as a browser parses it, against the WHATWG HTML standard, WAI-ARIA, the Vanilla Breeze vocabulary, and this project's house rules in `htmlverify.config.json`. A hook runs it after every write to an `.html` file, and its report comes back to you when the file fails. ## Workflow 1. Check: `npx htmlverify check page.html`. For a fragment, such as a component or a snippet, name the element it goes inside: `--context tbody`. 2. Apply the mechanical fixes: `npx htmlverify fix page.html --write`. They change only the form of the markup (quotes, case, `
`, boolean values, explicit tags, escaping, whitespace), never the parsed tree. 3. Fix the rest by hand, errors first. `npx htmlverify explain ` says why a rule exists and shows a failing and a passing example. 4. Check again. Stop after three rounds, or when the same finding survives two rounds, and report what remains. 5. Hand back the result with its status and its open review items. ## Reading a report - `error` fails the file; `warning` and `info` don't. - Each finding gives its rule, its position, and what to do. `[fix]` marks one that `fix` applies. - `review` lines are questions only a person can answer, such as whether an alt text describes its image. Pass them on to the user; never answer them yourself. - `untested` lists checks that didn't run. Don't claim they passed. ## Rules of engagement - Fix the cause, not the rule. Never turn rules off, lower their severity, or edit `htmlverify.config.json` to get a pass. - Never invent content to satisfy a check: no made-up alt text, labels, captions, titles, or review answers. Ask the user for the real content. - Use Vanilla Breeze elements and attributes as declared; the messages name the declared ones. Don't rename an element to an ad-hoc `x-*` one to get past `component/unknown-element`. - Prefer native HTML to ARIA on generic elements: `
